thread_tweets.text:
2Spectrum: the killer app(s)

Spectrum is the “first child” of @ColbySaysHi and the team @IroraCapital. Great and seasoned developers and good people trying to leave a mark and build their legacy. They led what has basically been a community rebirth in Prism, and done so creating a very simple primitive that is an absolute pillar of traditional finance somehow culpably absent in crypto so far: Indexes.

The 0 to 1 moment for @spectrumindexes will probably be when quality KOL start running the math on fees and launching their own basket: they’ll realize they can print infinite with a good basket, respawn the print higher and higher as volume scales, and doing it while providing a service to their audience instead of dumping bundled trash on their heads. 

Fee on the basket is to be selected by the person who launches it in a 1% to 3% range: the low range of what tardfi private funds or niche ETF and Indexes have been charging for decades.

30% goes to the Index launcher. 
20% buys and burns $Prism forever.

AND.

50% goes to basket holders. 

And this is what changes the whole value proposition: you are basically getting paid to hold your favourite index, instead of paying an annual fee. No one really understands the impilcations of that in depth: you now have an army of bagworkers automatically incentivized to work for your index, built in an evergrowing, eyeball attracting platform from day1.

Finally, because this is not a fucking gimmick, the basket is not synthetic liquidity: there is no “index amm” for phantom liquidity that can get rugges, this actually buys the underlying that is always redeemable by you 1:1 at any moment.
So it benefits projects included in the basket too. 

And that’s the last piece of the exponential puzzle: projects will WANT to be in there: volume, eyeballs, legitimacy if the Index is from respected big names. 

So you have the “ultimate bagworkers” in there too, the projects themselves, with whatever extra incentive they’ll wanna throw in the mix: extra yeld for DeFi’s all stars ETF? A TV spot for podcast show hosts baskets? Airdrops for NFT bros Index? 

No one cracked Indexes/ETF because tek, to some extent, sure, and now we have that. But also, frankly, mainly ‘cause greed: fees where never enough, there was always shady backroom deals, or some weird synthetic low liquidity pool to nuke, and why would holders ever be paid? But to work, this has to all be extremely simple, social, one click. Enter portfolio 👇

3Portfolio: AI and onboarding

Portfolio is the new addition to the equation. And shows once more how focused the team is on ux and the central importance it has for onboarding nocoiners. It’s basically a portfolio manager/creator. With advanced AI assist and automation. There are dozens of projects that do this out there, with no moat, sloppy execution, and hundreds of millions of mcap to vacuum. “Calling bullshit” is what Prism is doing here, again: you don’t need a whole new project, another KOL extraction, you really don’t need another token at all if you’re honest. This will be a nice change of pace and will give you better execution far beyond the 0.4% alone. Like we said you’ll blocktronics analytics on your holdings, a bloomber style news feed will be integrated later this year, a proper deck.

More. Agentic basket creation is now LIVE. In both the fact that you can have AI assisted basket creation, and also rhere are skills for your agent or claw to create indexes thenselves autonomously! As we nove forward, more and more agentic usage is projected, far surpassing human one. And this is futureproofing that.

The onboard flow is what matters to me here, once more, the simple stuff: slide a lever, and your private portfolio goes public miniting it as your own index in seconds. One click. 

And a whole social layer app is being built around that as well, leaderboards for the best portfolios, incentives: social trading is here to stay, and this is very clear to everyone at Prism.

Application software carries that whole load, and most of it is rated B- or lower. The parts AI helps, cybersecurity and infrastructure, carry a fraction: about $28B and $21B.

It's very common for founders not to know how well they're doing. In both directions. It's obviously common for founders to be making mistakes and not realize it. But it's also surprisingly common for them to be doing great and not realize it.

I think the reason is that running a startup is so unlike other kinds of work. By your third startup, you'd know if you were doing great. But with the first one you don't have anything to compare it to.

Want to know my secret for telling how well a startup is doing? What's their growth rate? That's the high bit, and in base 10. If their growth rate is good, unless it's good from giving away money, everything else must be good enough.

The market turns green for few days and suddenly the timeline is euphoric again, everyone posting their gains, everyone an expert.

Let me offer a different, more useful take: how to make the most out of the next 12 months.

First, understand where we are. This is the very beginning, not the end. When the timeline gets loud you assume it's a top signal, but the real top is when your barber, your Uber driver and your mom are asking which coin to buy. We are nowhere near that.

The single biggest mistake you can make right now is letting your bear market scars make your decisions for you.

After more than a year of everything bleeding, your instincts are broken. Every green candle feels like the top. Every 2x feels like a gift you need to grab before it disappears. So you sell, you take the small win, you feel relief, and then you watch the thing you sold do another 10x without you.

That's not risk management. That's just bear ptsd, and it will cost you this entire cycle.

In a bear market you're rewarded for caution. In a bull market you're rewarded for conviction. The hardest part is flipping your brain from one mode to the other at the right time, and most people flip far too late.

A few things that actually help:

Hold your highest conviction positions through the volatility. Your winners can run longer than you might think. Don't rotate out of a 3x into some "cheaper" play and miss the 20x.

But holding doesn't mean never taking profit. Have a plan for both directions before emotion decides for you. Sell on a plan, never on fear.

Trust the teams that shipped through the entire bear. Be far more careful with the ones that only appeared last week.

And accept that you will miss things. Coins you looked at will 50x without you. Let them go. Chasing what you missed is exactly how you buy tops.

You survived the longest bear market, which was the most difficult part. But now it’s time to make the most out of it.

Having said that, enjoy it. You earned what’s ahead of us.

From my « AI practitioner » point of view new chips are crucial.

Every AI company is extremely compute constrained. Imagine I have 100 million users who want to use my product, but with the compute available today, I can only serve 10 million of them.

The obvious answer is to add more compute. But compute is physical infrastructure. Chips, memory, networking, electricity, land, permits, and construction. Every part is a bottleneck.

So let’s say we can add one gigawatt of capacity every quarter. We are doing everything possible to add more, but in the short term that supply is basically fixed.

Now imagine the next generation of chips can produce 2 to 3 times more useful tokens per megawatt. Suddenly, with the exact same electricity and data center capacity, I can serve 2 to 3 times more users. That is massive.

Better models are another lever, and those better models also depend on having better chips for training. If today I need a one trillion parameter model to complete a task reliably, but the next generation can do the same task with a 300 billion parameter model, inference becomes much cheaper. I can serve more requests with the same compute and ultimately make more money from the same subscription price.

Then there is engineering. Context compaction, better context engineering, caching etc, and moving work away from GPUs whenever possible. We spend a lot of time squeezing efficiency out of every part of the stack obviously. 

But new chips remain one of the biggest levers. When electricity is the fixed constraint, the most valuable chip is the one that turns every megawatt into the largest number of useful tokens.

That’s why I’m so excited that Vera Rubin will now be available on Azure!

Reflecting on my agent stack, so much has been commoditized since May. ChatGPT and Claude can now send emails, create calendar invites, and search Google Drive. No need for a complex CLI setup or a laptop running 24/7. It all works from mobile!

The main missing piece is SMS, WhatsApp, and Telegram. That’s basically the last reason I still need Codex or Claude Code running on a laptop. I also use Computer use like right now my agent is selling a couch on Facebook Marketplace.

My wife recently subscribed to ChatGPT and connected her email, Drive, and calendar. It’s been a game changer. Our life is pretty well organized in Drive, so if she needs something about the car, finances, paperwork, etc., she can just ask and ChatGPT finds it.

Also interesting how far ahead work agents are. Copilot Cowork can use Microsoft Graph to work across Outlook, SharePoint, OneDrive, DynamicsCRM etc. and handle workflows end to end. I guess it makes sense because Enterprise customers pay more, so they get these agentic experiences first. Then they slowly make their way to consumers.
